reasons: Lake identity is verified for Soldal v. Cook County, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1992-12-08, year 1992.
The payload's parallel and vendor-neutral citations match the lake citation lists; the lake has official/display citation null, matching the blank citation field and official_citation_present=false.
residual_risks: Lake provenance warns that official cite selection failed, but under the disclosed lake record the asserted metadata matches.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If the citation policy later treats 506 U.S. 56 as the display cite, revise the citation/display field consistently.

reasons: The opinion states that a property seizure occurs when there is meaningful interference with possessory interests.
The opinion rejects the view that Fourth Amendment property protection depends on an invasion of privacy or liberty.
residual_risks: Footnote 7 cautions that the Amendment does not protect possessory interests in all kinds of property.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Say 'Fourth-Amendment-covered property interests, including houses and effects' if the corpus wants to avoid an all-property reading.

defect.locator_note: content_page.md Appears on section conflicts with the reviewed home_role payload/frontmatter.
defect.problem: The reviewed Trespass role is supportable only as related/cross-doctrine, but the built page's Appears on section assigns Trespass the stronger Key — Anchor role, creating an internal role conflict.
defect.proposed_fix: Synchronize the body Appears on entry for Trespass to 'Related (cross-doctrine)' or remove the conflicting body role.

reasons: The opinion includes a requested criminal trespass complaint and unlawful physical removal, which is enough for a related cross-doctrine placement.
The opinion's actual holding is seizure of property, not trespass as an anchor doctrine.
residual_risks: Do not promote Soldal as a Trespass anchor without a separate corpus rationale.

reasons: The opinion repeatedly contrasts property seizure with privacy and liberty/person interests, supporting only a cross-doctrine relation.
The role is not framed as a key seizure-of-person holding.
residual_risks: Soldal is not a seizure-of-the-person case; upgrading this role would overclaim.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the role limited to Related (cross-doctrine).

defect.locator_note: content_page.md frontmatter has Seizure of Property as Key — Anchor, but the body Appears on list does not.
defect.problem: The Seizure of Property anchor role is strongly supported, but the built page's Appears on section omits Seizure of Property and instead puts the anchor label under Trespass.
defect.proposed_fix: Add '[[Seizure of Property]] — Key — Anchor (seizure of property)' to the Appears on section and remove that anchor label from Trespass.

reasons: The opinion holds that physically tearing the trailer from its foundation and towing it away sufficed to constitute a Fourth Amendment seizure.
The lake scope note and opinion support Soldal as an anchor authority for seizure of property independent of privacy or liberty.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Synchronize frontmatter and body home-role displays.

residual_risks: Treatment edges and audit significance are for Lens B, not this support/quote-fidelity review.
